## Decisions and proofs
- Employee sampling: two independent uniform 16-bit values biject onto 2^32 outcomes. L=4294800000 leaves exactly 167296 rejected outcomes for bound 300000; retained residue counts are equal. Partial Fisher–Yates gives uniform ordered k-tuples and hence uniform subsets. Sparse map method needs implicit identity, as stated. Unpredictability and auditing are distinct from uniformity; no real giveaway was performed.
- Fermi: 30000*H/24 yields 7500/10000/12500 for hypothetical 6/8/10 hours. Flight-rate times residence-time model uses airborne, not ground, time. Daily average is explicitly not a live instantaneous count.
- Gold: subset enumeration reaches all 0..7 with 1,2,4 and 0..15 with 1,2,4,8. 2^k state lower bound makes 3/4 pieces necessary. Daily swap table matches binary balances. Cut counts assume one existing segment per cut, exchange allowed and proportional value.
- Horse 64: independently enumerated ALL 1680 linear extensions of the exact nine-candidate partial order after group/champion races, checking all three omitted-horse strategies. Ten/eleven-race branch counts were A4 1540/140, B3 1400/280, B1 1600/80. Each returns exactly the top-three remaining set with no ninth participant. Counts over this chosen finite order model are NOT real-world probabilities. B1 strategy guarantees membership, not always internal order. At-most-11 claim properly does not claim a global lower bound.
- Horse 25/36: seven/eight-race constructions use the five candidates A2,A3,B1,B2,C1. Independently scrutinized adversary lower bound: in k+1 races to eliminate k^2-1 unbeaten candidates each race must have k unbeaten runners. Losers never reappear. Adversary keeps a previous winner winning whenever present; final champion has at least two victories. Race runner-up U and third W, and another race runner-up V, have only champion (and U for W) known ahead, and V is incomparable with U,W. Linear extensions champion,U,W,V and champion,U,V,W yield different top-three sets, proving k+1 cannot guarantee the set, not merely order. This depends on fixed distinct speeds/full local ranks/no global timing. Ambiguous lane observations remain explicitly unresolved.
- Pirates: independent recurrence covers 1..10 participants for >=half and strict-majority thresholds, including dead=-1 distinct from live zero, stable individual identity, equal-pay rejection, own vote and integer coins. Both displayed ten-person vectors and intermediate rows match; votes and conservation checked. Tied cheapest voters permit nonunique allocations.
- Guide: complete original question/model/numeric scope retained; headings now say what to check rather than implying a hidden complete implementation. Java 21/module/script names are historical verification organization and clearly cannot be run from this page. Reading-note warning survives actual pager. Guide's egg/coin/water/geometry names reference broader study topics, not newly verified executable deliverables here.
- Ring: nine-state recurrence agrees with independent binomial displacement sum for n=0..60, including odd n=9 with two paths. Empty path, Java negative remainder and exact arithmetic requirements retained. O(9n)/O(9) are arithmetic-operation/count-state bounds, not constant-bit-cost guarantees for arbitrary BigInteger sizes.
- Shots: independent DP reproduces 9528805 (0..10) and 9091270 (1..10), with inclusion-exclusion cross-check. Unordered multiplicities cannot be obtained by dividing by 10!.
- Shooters: enumerated all eight simultaneous first-round hit outcomes into exact probabilities 0.192/0.152/0.048/0.608. Exact absorbing-state solution gives 144/1309,9/119,904/1309,162/1309 and total 1. Second-round survival numbers are nonexclusive events, unlike eventual absorption. Generic p=q=0 boundary added. No equilibrium or universal weak-shooter optimality claim.
